title: Conditional Advantage Estimation for Reinforcement Learning in Large Reasoning Models
claim: Prior advantage estimation compares each response to a single global mean; ours regroups by a metric and compares between and within groups.
layout: 2 panels split by dashed line, left prior, right ours, formulas below
description: The figure is split by a vertical dashed line. The left panel, DR.GRPO, shows a query q branching into four sampled responses o1 to o4. Each response is a row of small hand-drawn squares, yellow for correct and red for incorrect, ending in a green check or red cross. A single group mean of 0.75 gives advantages 0.25, 0.25, -0.75 and 0.25. The right panel, CANON, regroups the same responses by entropy from lower to higher using a double-headed arrow. A horizontal line divides the lower-entropy group G-q from the higher-entropy group G+q. Arrows labelled Inter and Intra lead to two numeric columns of inter-group and intra-group advantages. Dashed lines separate the bottom row of formulas. On the left, DR.GRPO's formula is written with a pink note that it equals half the inter term plus half the intra term. On the right are the piecewise formulas for inter and intra advantage.
caption: CANON amplifies the impact of specific metric changes by regrouping the sampled responses into two groups based on the values of a given metric. Rather than comparing against the mean value of all responses like DR.GRPO, CANON selects the direction of metric change that offers greater contributions to performance through inter-group comparison and favors responses that exhibit better performance within groups following the same trend in its intra-group comparison. DR.GRPO can be expressed as the average of CANON’s two advantage estimates and is therefore a special case of CANON.
abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for large language models (LLMs) has achieved remarkable progress in enhancing LLMs' reasoning capabilities on tasks with clear correctness criteria, such as mathematical reasoning tasks. Several training metrics, such as entropy or response length, have been observed to correlate with different reasoning behaviors in reinforcement learning. Prior approaches incorporate such priors through reward or advantage shaping, which often relies on hand-crafted penalties and preferences (e.g., higher-is-better or lower-is-better). However, without careful hyperparameter tuning, these directional priors can be overly biased and may lead to failure. To this end, we introduce Conditional advANtage estimatiON (CANON), amplifying the impact of the target metric without presuming its direction. Specifically, CANON regroups the sampled responses into two groups based on the higher or lower value of a target metric, measures which metric trend contributes to better performance through inter-group comparison, and identifies the better response within the same group. In summary, CANON based on entropy consistently outperforms prior methods across three LLMs on both math reasoning and high-complexity logic tasks. When applied to response length, CANON further improves token efficiency, yielding a more favorable Pareto frontier in the performance-cost trade-off.
